dataGaps: No official annual series of farmland converted to urban or other uses (by change-of-vocation decision or by remote sensing), nationally or by governorate; Ministry of Agriculture, ONAGRI and INS searched without result. The only national estimate specific to urbanisation (2,000-3,000 ha/yr) is a secondary citation of the 2012 Euronet environmental profile, which was not opened.

The DGAT study (1,370 ha changed vocation 2011-2021) and the AUGT studies on construction in prohibition zones (Manouba 66.5%, Ben Arous ~35%, Ariana >50%) are known only through press; originals not found, geography and denominators unclear.

No national peer-reviewed land-cover change study (e.g. Landsat 1985-2020) quantifying cropland converted to built-up land was found; Sfax (olive 'jnens') and the Sahel (Sousse, Monastir) lack quantified studies beyond Kalâa Kebira.

No sourced projection of future farmland loss to urbanisation. Only press statements on urban land demand exist (AFH target of 15,000 ha serviced by 2030 with a regional breakdown summing to 22,500 ha; ministry statement of 17,000 ha housing needs by 2030), with no share on farmland. No predicted finding was written.
Elloumi 2011 (CIHEAM Options Méditerranéennes B66) and Gafsi 1996 could not be downloaded (host unreachable / 404), so the method behind the mid-1990s 23,000 ha/yr estimate is unknown.
The Ministry of Environment's 2022 national state-of-environment report (Arabic PDF) was downloaded but its text layer is unreadable.
Whether marginal land (rangeland, new olive plantations) is being added while peri-urban land is lost is a hypothesis; no source links the two.
Loss of farm output and income attributable to conversion (e.g. vegetables and milk supply around Tunis) is not quantified.

excerpt: Tunisia's coastal towns grow mostly onto the farmland around them, which is often the most fertile and best-watered land. In Greater Tunis, 2,440 of the 3,970 ha urbanised between 1986 and 1991 were farmland. The…

sections.heading: Problem
sections.content:
Tunisia's coastal towns grow mostly onto the farmland around them, which is often the most fertile and best-watered land. In Greater Tunis, 2,440 of the 3,970 ha urbanised between 1986 and 1991 were farmland (SRC-TG-845, citing Gafsi 1996). The government's 2016 Habitat III report says informal building has spread over fertile farmland. It also says public facilities and economic projects take about 400 ha of farmland a year through separate changes of vocation (SRC-TG-846). A 2018 CIHEAM chapter, citing the 2012 environmental profile of Tunisia, puts urban losses at 2,000-3,000 ha of farmland a year (SRC-TG-854).

Local remote-sensing studies show the same pattern in Cap Bon and the Sahel:
- Kelibia (Nabeul), 2012-2016: built-up area on farmland grew from 13 to 44 ha (SRC-TG-847).
- Kalâa Kebira (Sousse), 2012-2023: urban area grew from 890 to 1,307 ha while tree crops lost 621 ha (SRC-TG-848).

There is no official series. The figures that circulate range from 137 to 25,000 ha a year, because they measure different things.

sections.heading: Root causes
sections.content:
The symptom is farmland turned into housing, industry and infrastructure. The causes named in the sources are below.

- **Past housing and land policy (legacy decision).** A ministry-commissioned diagnosis says housing programmes since the 1970s caused the loss and fragmentation of thousands of hectares of fertile farmland, worst in Greater Tunis. It also says public operators' sector logic, including the AFH's pressure to develop land reserves bought very cheaply in the 1970s, often overrode planning (SRC-TG-845). Formal serviced land stayed small: the AFH serviced 1,094 ha in 1995-2014, about 55 ha a year nationwide (SRC-TG-846). The same report names a weak housing policy for low-income groups as a cause of sprawl (SRC-TG-846, p. 20). It is our inference from those pages, not the report's own words, that small formal supply pushed households into informal subdivisions on farmland. The report itself credits the AFH's subdivisions with reducing unplanned sprawl onto farmland (SRC-TG-846, p. 21). The 2014 diagnosis adds that the declassification procedure is too slow to get ahead of informal housing (SRC-TG-845).
- **Siting public and economic projects on farmland case by case.** Public facilities and economic projects are placed on farmland through separate changes of vocation, which also encourages informal building around them (SRC-TG-846). The 400 ha/yr figure measures the result of this practice, not its cause. The legal mechanism is described in FND-TG-841.
- **Coastal concentration.** The north-east and centre-east, 17.2% of the territory, hold about 61.6% of the population. The government links this to intense pressure on fertile farmland, alongside a weak national spatial-planning strategy and ineffective planning tools (SRC-TG-846).
- **Weak local institutions and non-binding plans.** Municipalities have weak technical means (SRC-TG-846). The urbanisation zones in regional master plans (SDA) "ne revêtent pas de caractère obligatoire" (are not binding) and are disconnected from municipal needs (SRC-TG-845, p. 30). Public land perimeters (PIF) were created outside urban plans on farmland: Ennasr II in Ariana started in 1987, but the land was declassified only in 1993 (SRC-TG-845).

sections.heading: Evidence
sections.content:
**What is solid.** Official, institutional and peer-reviewed sources agree that urbanisation in coastal regions takes farmland (SRC-TG-845, SRC-TG-846, SRC-TG-847, SRC-TG-854). Peri-urban land around Greater Tunis includes irrigated land, such as the lower Medjerda perimeter built in the 1950s (SRC-TG-854). For Greater Tunis in 1986-1991, 61% of the land urbanised (2,440 of 3,970 ha) was farmland (SRC-TG-845, secondary citation of Gafsi 1996). For Gabès, the same report cites a thesis: water competition plus unplanned urbanisation caused the loss of nearly 60% of the oasis's farmland, with no period given (SRC-TG-845, citing Abdedaiem 2009).

**Rates disagree, and they measure different things:**
- 2,000-3,000 ha/yr of farmland lost to urban pressure, around 2012, as a separate figure from 15,000-20,000 ha/yr lost to erosion. This is a secondary citation of the EU-funded 2012 environmental profile, which was not opened (SRC-TG-854).
- About 400 ha/yr of farmland changed vocation for public facilities and economic projects (Habitat III national report, 2016; no stated period or method) (SRC-TG-846).
- 1,370 ha changed vocation in 2011-2021, about 137 ha/yr, from an ongoing DGAT study known only through press, with unclear geography (SRC-TG-850). If national, it is well below the 400 ha/yr in SRC-TG-846.
- About 4,000 ha/yr of urban land consumption (no year stated; La Presse article of 18 May 2026), nearly 40% of it unplanned. This is an expert's figure reported in the press, and it covers all land types, not only farmland (SRC-TG-852).
- "Over 20,000 ha/yr" (SRC-TG-850), "25,000 ha/yr" (SRC-TG-851) and "about 23,000 ha/yr estimated in the mid-1990s" (SRC-TG-850) are total farmland losses from erosion and urbanisation combined. The Nawaat paragraph is footnoted to Elloumi (2011, CIHEAM), which could not be opened.

The change-of-vocation figures cover only formal decisions and miss informal building, which probably explains part of the gap with the 2,000-3,000 ha/yr estimate.

**The common belief does not hold as stated.** The often-quoted 20,000-25,000 ha/yr is not a measure of land lost to urbanisation. It combines erosion with urbanisation, and the one source that separates them attributes most of it to erosion (15,000-20,000 ha/yr) and only 2,000-3,000 ha/yr to urban pressure (SRC-TG-854). It is roughly 50 to 180 times the formal change-of-vocation figures above. That the later press figures descend from the mid-1990s estimate is our inference from the similar magnitudes and Nawaat's wording (SRC-TG-850).

**National aggregates do not show the loss.** FAO-based agricultural land (arable land, permanent crops and pasture) rose from 90,610 km2 in 1980 to 100,380 km2 in 2010, then eased to 96,469 km2 in 2023 (SRC-TG-849). Arable land fell from 3.19 Mha in 1980 to 2.77 Mha in 2023, but the series does not attribute the change to any cause (SRC-TG-849). The loss is concentrated on fertile, irrigated, near-market land. We hypothesise, without a source linking the two, that marginal land such as rangeland or new olive plantations is being added elsewhere and masks it in the totals. A soil-loss framing does not fit this evidence, so the theme is land-structure.

**Local case studies (Cap Bon, Sahel):**
- **Kelibia, Nabeul, 2012-2016:** urban area grew from 458 to 756 ha; built-up area on farmland from 13 to 44 ha (Table 7 for 458 to 756 ha; Table 5 for 13 to 44 ha). The "400%" stated in the paper's text does not match its table (SRC-TG-847).
- **Kalâa Kebira, Sousse, 2012-2023:** urban area +417 ha (890 to 1,307 ha); tree crops -621 ha; mixed crops -111 ha; pasture and uncultivated land +315 ha. Urbanisation explains only part of the crop loss; drought and abandonment also play a role. The source is an unreviewed preprint with internal errors (SRC-TG-848).
- **Manouba, Ben Arous, Ariana:** the press cites AUGT studies giving the share of construction in protected zones as 66.5%, about 35% and over 50%. The base of these percentages is unclear (SRC-TG-850).

sections.heading: Why confidence is what it is
sections.content:
Confidence that the problem exists and in which direction it runs is medium. A government report (SRC-TG-846), a ministry-commissioned diagnosis (SRC-TG-845), a CIHEAM chapter (SRC-TG-854) and a peer-reviewed study (SRC-TG-847) agree, and the official gazette shows conversions happening (FND-TG-841).

Confidence in any rate is low:
- The only urbanisation-specific national estimate (2,000-3,000 ha/yr) is a secondary citation of a 2012 consultancy report that was not opened.
- The 400 ha/yr is one undated government figure.
- The other rates come from the press.
- The Greater Tunis and Gabès figures are secondary citations, and the Kalâa Kebira study is a preprint with errors.
- Sfax and the Sahel beyond Kalâa Kebira are not quantified.

Severity is set at medium because the national farmland base is not shrinking measurably. The loss falls on high-value peri-urban and irrigated land, so local severity is likely higher.

sections.heading: Links to other sectors
sections.content:
**Water.** Peri-urban land lost around Greater Tunis includes irrigated land, such as the lower Medjerda perimeter (SRC-TG-854). Safeguard zones are defined partly by irrigation and exploitable groundwater, and prohibition zones include public irrigated perimeters (SRC-TG-840). Building on these lands wastes public irrigation investment. Further links:
- The press reports a large share of Manouba construction in prohibition zones, i.e. public irrigated perimeters or forest (SRC-TG-850).
- In Gabès, urbanisation combined with competition for water is linked to the loss of nearly 60% of oasis farmland (SRC-TG-845).
- The Kelibia study links building in the hydraulic public domain to flooding vulnerability (SRC-TG-847), and the Habitat III report links sprawl to more frequent urban flooding (SRC-TG-846).

Water-lane researchers may want to quantify the irrigated perimeter area lost to building.

**Energy.** None found beyond individual conversions for grid infrastructure (see FND-TG-841).

sections.heading: Leads for phase 2
sections.content:
- Law 83-87 on the protection of agricultural land and its amendments: https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/tun13870.pdf (see FND-TG-841)
- Agricultural land protection maps per governorate (cartes de protection des terres agricoles), cited in SRC-TG-843
- Planning instruments under the Code de l'aménagement du territoire et de l'urbanisme (law 94-122): SDA, PAU, PIF
- AFH serviced-land programmes (e.g. Jardins de Tunis, 331 ha; Ezzahra-Rades, 264 ha), cited in SRC-TG-846
- New national housing strategy 2025-2035 (in preparation per press): https://www.leconomistemaghrebin.com/2024/07/14/tunisie-prepare-une-nouvelle-strategie-nationale-de-habitat-pour-periode-2025-2035/
- Urban densification and in-fill policy (intensification of existing urban fabric), mentioned in SRC-TG-846
- Remote-sensing monitoring of urban growth (Pleiades / Landsat methods in SRC-TG-847, SRC-TG-848)
- Profil environnemental de la Tunisie (Euronet Consortium, 2012), cited in SRC-TG-854

sections.heading: Verification
sections.content:
Headline figures and indicators were traced to the cited copies (CIHEAM Mediterra 2018 ch. 8, Mehat 2014 report, Habitat III national report, Kassouk 2022, Ghenimi preprint, World Bank WDI API, press articles).

**Independent review, 21 November 2026:** pass after corrections. Checked: SRC-TG-854 ch. 8 (2,000-3,000 and 15,000-20,000 ha/yr, as stated by that chapter; Euronet 2012 itself not opened), SRC-TG-845 section "Accès au foncier" (3,970 and 2,440 ha), SRC-TG-846 (400 ha/yr; 61.6% and 17.2%; AFH 1,094 ha), SRC-TG-847 Tables 5 and 7, SRC-TG-848 Table 2, SRC-TG-849 World Bank API (1980, 2010, 2023), SRC-TG-850 and SRC-TG-851 articles, SRC-TG-852 article. Corrections: urban land consumption year "c. 2025" changed to "not stated in source (article dated 18 May 2026)"; Kelibia locator corrected to Table 7 (458 to 756 ha) and Table 5 (13 to 44 ha). Independent teammate sign-off is outstanding; reviewer and author share the TahaGHZ identity, so the record is not validated.

resolvedSources.title: Loi n° 83-87 du 11 novembre 1983 relative à la protection des terres agricoles (original text)
resolvedSources.publisher: République Tunisienne, Journal Officiel (JORT n° 74, 15-18 novembre 1983, p. 2920-2921); copy hosted by FAO FAOLEX
resolvedSources.extracts:
Article 1:

> On entend par terres agricoles au sens de la présente loi, toutes les terres présentant des potentialités physiques et affectées ou pouvant être le support d'une production agricole, forestière ou pastorale, ainsi que celles qui sont classées comme telles par les plans d'aménagement dûment approuvés, dans les zones urbaines, touristiques ou industrielles.

English gloss: agricultural land means all land with physical potential that is or could be used for crop, forest or pastoral production, plus land classed as agricultural in approved development plans.

Article 3:

> Les terres agricoles telles que définies à l'Article 1er de la présente loi sont réparties en trois zones: - Zone d'interdiction - Zone de sauvegarde - Zone soumise à autorisation

English gloss: agricultural land is divided into three zones: prohibition, safeguard, and zone subject to authorisation.

Article 4 (extract):

> Les zones d'interdiction couvrent les terres agricoles destinées à demeurer comme telles, et comprennent les périmètres publics irrigués [...] ainsi que les terres forestières relevant du domaine forestier de l'Etat [...]. Dans ces zones, la modificatin de la vocation des terres agricoles ne peut être opérée que dans le cadre des lois particulières les régissant.

English gloss: prohibition zones cover land meant to stay agricultural, including public irrigated perimeters and state forest land; their use can only change under the special laws that govern them.

Article 5 (extract):

> Les zones de sauvegarde couvrent les terres dont la vacation agricole doit être protégée en raison de leur impact sur la production agricole nationale. [...] - les oasis, [...] - les forêts d'oliviers et les grands ensembles complantés dans le cadre de projets nationaux ou régionaux, - les zones à dominante arboriculture fruitière, - les terres présentant des potentialités agricoles importantes notamment en raison de l'existence de nappes d'eau souterraines eploitables ou de la fertilité de leur sol,

English gloss: safeguard zones protect land important to national production, including irrigated land, oases, olive "forests", fruit-tree areas, and land with exploitable groundwater or fertile soil.

Article 6 (extract):

> Les zones de sauvegarde sont fixées pour chaque gouvernorat par décret pris sur proposition du Ministre de l'Agriculture et après avis de la commission technique consultative régionale des terres agricoles [...]. Toute modification des zones de sauvegarde doit intevenir dans les conditions fixées à l'alinéa précédent.

English gloss: safeguard zones are fixed per governorate by decree, and can be modified by the same procedure (a decree).

Article 8 (extract):

> Tout changement de vocation des terres comprises dans ces zones est soumis à l'autorisation préalable du Ministre de l'Agriculture délivrée par arrêté.

English gloss: in the remaining agricultural zones, any change of use needs prior authorisation from the Minister of Agriculture, issued by order (arrêté).

Article 9 (extract):

> Dans ce cadre, toute nouvelle agglomération, sera implantée sur les terres les moins fertiles.

English gloss: any new settlement shall be located on the least fertile land.

Article 13 (extract):

> les mêmes autorités peuvent procéder aux frais et risques du contrevenant à la démolition de la construction

English gloss: the authorities "may" demolish unauthorised construction at the offender's cost.

Article 14:

> Les infractins aux dispositins de la présente loi et des textes pris pour son application, seront punies: - d'une amende de l.200 à 10.000 dinars pour les infractions commises dans les zones d'interdictin et de sauvegarde. - d'une amende de 120 à 1.200 dinars pour les infractions commises dans les zones soumises dans les zones soumises à autorisatin ministérielle.

English gloss: the 1983 penalties were fines only: 1,200 to 10,000 dinars in prohibition and safeguard zones, 120 to 1,200 dinars in the authorisation zone.
resolvedSources.notes: FAOLEX retyped text (not a scan of the gazette); typos are reproduced as found. Gazette reference taken from the FAOLEX record. Articles 3, 8, 9, 13, 14 and part of 10 were later replaced by law 96-104 (SRC-TG-842) and article 11 by law 90-45 (SRC-TG-841).

resolvedSources.title: JORT 2022: arrêté of 24 March 2022 (Ben Arous) and Décret Présidentiel n° 2022-57 of 26 January 2022 (Sfax) changing the vocation of agricultural plots
resolvedSources.publisher: République Tunisienne, Journal Officiel (n° 36, 1er avril 2022, p. 884; n° 12, 1er février 2022, p. 326-327); scans hosted by FAO FAOLEX
resolvedSources.extracts:
Second document URL: https://faolex.fao.org/docs/pdf/tun208166.pdf

Arrêté du 24 mars 2022 (JORT n° 36, 1er avril 2022, p. 884), visas:

> Vu la loi n° 83-87 du 11 novembre 1983, relative à la protection des terres agricoles, ensemble les textes qui l'ont modifié et complété et notamment la loi n° 2019-47 du 29 mai 2019 relative à l'amélioration du climat de l'investissement,

> Vu l'avis de la commission technique consultative régionale des terres agricoles du gouvernorat de Ben Arous, consigné dans son procès-verbal du 24 septembre 2019.

Article premier:

> Est changée la vocation de la parcelle de terre agricole, d'une superficie de 1 ha 33 ares 35 ca objet du titre foncier n° 72404 Ben Arous sise à la délégation de Mhamdia du gouvernorat de Ben Arous, et classée en autres zones agricoles [...] et ce, pour la création d'une unité de fabrication des cartables scolaires.

English gloss: the joint order of the agriculture and equipment ministers converts a 1.33 ha plot in "other agricultural zones" (Mhamdia, Ben Arous) to build a school-bag factory. The regional commission's opinion dates from 24 September 2019, the order from 24 March 2022 (about 2.5 years later). The law 83-87 is cited as amended "notably" by law 2019-47 on the investment climate.

Décret Présidentiel n° 2022-57 du 26 janvier 2022 (JORT n° 12, 1er février 2022, p. 326), article premier:

> Est changée la vocation de la parcelle de terre agricole objet de titre foncier n° 132041 Sfax, classée en zones de sauvegarde, d'une superficie de 01 ha 40 ares 05 ca et sise à la délégation de Sakiet Ezzit du gouvernorat de Sfax [...] pour la création d'un poste de transformation de haute et moyenne tension. Sont modifiées en conséquence [...] les limites des zones de sauvegarde des terres agricoles du gouvernorat de Sfax fixées par le décret n° 2007-2740 du 31 octobre 2007.

English gloss: a presidential decree converts a 1.40 ha plot classified as safeguard zone in Sakiet Ezzit (Sfax) for a high/medium-voltage substation, and redraws the Sfax safeguard-zone limits accordingly.
resolvedSources.notes: Two individual cases; they show the procedure (plot-by-plot decree or arrêté, safeguard-zone limits amended by the same text), not the scale of conversion. The text of law 2019-47 itself was not opened.

resolvedSources.title: Pour une nouvelle stratégie de l'habitat: Accès au foncier. Rapport provisoire, diagnostics et recommandations
resolvedSources.publisher: Ministère de l'Equipement, de l'Aménagement du Territoire et du Développement Durable (consultant Hend Ben Othman Bacha)
resolvedSources.extracts:
Section II.2, p. 29:

> Sur les 16,3 millions d'hectares que compte la Tunisie, 10 millions d'hectares sont des terres agricoles réparties entre des terrains forestiers ( 1,2 millions HA), des terres « raaouia » (3,5 millions HA), et 5,3 millions HA cultivables dont 0,5 millions d'ha sont des périmètres irrigués.

English gloss: of Tunisia's 16.3 Mha, 10 Mha are agricultural (1.2 Mha forest, 3.5 Mha rangeland, 5.3 Mha cultivable of which 0.5 Mha irrigated perimeters). Footnote 32 cites Laassidi A., 2014, ministry training material.

p. 29:

> La mise en oeuvre des différents programmes d'habitat depuis les années 1970 a abouti à la perte et au mitage de milliers d'hectares de terres agricoles fertiles. Le Grand Tunis est le plus touché par ces pertes, où l'extension urbaine s'est fait essentiellement aux dépens des terres agricoles. Entre 1986 et 1991, les superficies urbanisées dans le grand Tunis se répartissent comme suit : (i) 2 440 ha de sol agricole, (ii) 1 160 ha de sol nu, 370 ha de berges de lac et de sebkhas, soit un total de 3 970 ha, donc essentiellement sur des terres agricoles.

English gloss: housing programmes since the 1970s caused the loss and fragmentation of thousands of hectares of fertile farmland, worst in Greater Tunis. In 1986-1991, 3,970 ha were urbanised in Greater Tunis, of which 2,440 ha agricultural land. Footnote 33: Gafsi H. (1996), in Ben Ali D. et al., Urbanisation et agriculture en Méditerranée, L'Harmattan-CIHEAM, p. 55-70 (secondary citation).

p. 29:

> Dans le cas de l'oasis de Gabès, selon S. Abdedaiem, la conjugaison des deux facteurs, concurrence sur la ressource en eau et mitage de l'espace oasien par une urbanisation anarchique, ont abouti à la perte de près de 60 % des terres agricoles.

English gloss: in the Gabès oasis, water competition plus unplanned urbanisation led to the loss of nearly 60% of farmland (citing Abdedaiem, 2009 thesis; secondary citation, no period given).

p. 30, on PIF (land intervention perimeters):

> rien dans les textes n'interdit la création de ces PIF en dehors des PAU. Cette ambiguïté dans les textes réglementaires a laissé la porte ouverte à la création de Pif qui sont généralement en dehors du périmètre communal sur des zones agricole, tel qu'Ennasr II à l'Ariana qui a démarré en 1987, alors que le déclassement de la zone en question n'est intervenu qu'en 1993

English gloss: nothing prevents public land-intervention perimeters outside urban plans; e.g. Ennasr II (Ariana) started in 1987 while the land was only declassified in 1993.

p. 30, on regional master plans (SDA):

> les orientations des SDA sont d'une part déconnectées des réels besoins des communes en zones agricoles à déclasser et d'autre part les zones définies pour l'urbanisation à moyen et long terme, même si elles doivent être respectées par les PAU, ne revêtent pas de caractère obligatoire et ne sont que formelles

English gloss: SDA orientations are disconnected from municipalities' real needs for land to declassify, and the zones they set for medium- and long-term urbanisation are not binding and only formal.

p. 31, on public operators:

> La logique sectorielle de l'opérateur public l'emporte souvent sur la vision stratégique des planificateurs, et ce en raison des besoins en terrains pour satisfaire les demandes en logements croissantes et des pressions de l'AFH pour valoriser des réserves foncières acquises dans les années 1970, à des prix très bas.

English gloss: the public operator's sector logic often overrides planners' strategy, because of land needs for growing housing demand and AFH pressure to develop land reserves bought very cheaply in the 1970s.

p. 30, procedure:

> la procédure de déclassement est longue et ne permet pas d'anticiper l'avancée de l'habitat spontané qui se fait généralement aux dépens de ces terrains en friches mais revêtant encore le caractère agricole.

English gloss: the declassification procedure is slow and cannot anticipate informal housing, which spreads over idle land still classed agricultural.

p. 31, "Des pratiques dérogatoires":

> Malgré la non intégration dans le périmètre urbain de ces terrains, des milliers d'hectares ont été déclassés au coup par coup, et ce en dehors ou à l'intérieur des périmètres communaux, sans aucun respect pour les instruments de planification urbaine

> le déclassement non judicieux de certaines zones, se faisait avant 2011 également au profit de certains acteurs privés, qui sont proches des cercles du pouvoir, contre l'avis des administrations concernées, pour des raisons spéculatives

English gloss: thousands of hectares were declassified case by case, ignoring urban plans; before 2011 some declassifications benefited private actors close to power, against the opinion of the administrations, for speculation (consultant's assessment).

p. 31, "Une loi pas assez coercitive":

> Les mesures prises contre le changement de vocation des terres agricoles sont peu dissuasives lors de la violation de la loi. En effet, les sanctions d'emprisonnement ne sont valables qu'en cas de construction sur les terres d'interdiction et de sauvegarde, celles portant sur les autres terres agricoles ne sont que financières, et limitée à 15000 DT, ce qui est très peu élevé compte tenu de la plus value opérée par le spéculateur

English gloss: penalties deter little; the report states prison applies only in prohibition and safeguard zones, and elsewhere only a fine capped at 15,000 DT, small compared with the speculator's gain.

p. 30, on the third category:

> Dans la pratique, le diagnostic montre que ces dispositifs comportent des insuffisances qui ont conduit à un étalement urbain non contrôlé et à un surenchérissement des prix fonciers.

English gloss: in practice these tools have led to uncontrolled sprawl and rising land prices.
resolvedSources.notes: Provisional consultant report for the housing strategy, published on the ministry website. Several figures are secondary citations (Gafsi 1996, Abdedaiem 2009, Laassidi 2014). Its reading of the penalties differs from the text of law 96-104 (SRC-TG-842), which allows prison in all zones and makes it mandatory only in prohibition and safeguard zones; the gazette text prevails.

resolvedSources.title: Habitat III: Rapport national de la troisième conférence des Nations Unies (Tunisie)
resolvedSources.publisher: République Tunisienne (national report submitted to UN Habitat III, Quito, October 2016)
resolvedSources.extracts:
p. 11 (section on urban demography):

> les régions du Nord-Est et du Centre-Est qui représentent 17,2% de la superficie du territoire national, a attiré environ 61,6% des habitants, ce qui a contribué de façon significative à faire une pression intense sur les écosystèmes fragiles, le littoral et les terres agricoles fertiles, surtout avec la présence, d'une part de la faiblesse de la stratégie nationale de l'aménagement du territoire et, d'autre part, l'inefficience des outils de la planification urbaine.

English gloss: the north-east and centre-east (17.2% of the territory) hold about 61.6% of the population, putting intense pressure on fertile farmland, worsened by a weak national spatial strategy and ineffective planning tools.

p. 15:

> Le pays a enregistré une intensification de la pression sur les ressources naturelles disponibles accompagnée d'une propagation concomitante de la construction anarchique au détriment des terres agricoles fertiles.

English gloss: informal construction has spread at the expense of fertile farmland.

p. 20, causes of urban sprawl:

> - La faiblesse des moyens techniques et matériels de la plupart des communes [...] - La faiblesse de la politique de l'habitat ciblant les catégories à faible revenu et les démunis [...] - La réalisation de certains équipements publics et projets économiques sur des terres agricoles dont la vocation sera changée séparément à raison de 400 hectares par an encourageant ainsi la prolifération des constructions anarchiques tout autour.

p. 20 (continued):

> Cet étalement désordonné et continu des villes a engendré des impacts négatifs sur l'espace urbain. La plupart des agglomérations urbaines ont connu une augmentation du rythme des inondations au sein de leurs quartiers et à leur périphérie

English gloss (both extracts): sprawl is caused by weak municipal means, a weak housing policy for low-income groups, and public facilities and economic projects built on farmland whose vocation is changed one by one at a rate of 400 ha per year, which encourages informal building around them. This disorderly sprawl has increased the frequency of flooding in most urban areas and their outskirts.

p. 21:

> L'Agence Foncière d'Habitation, principal intervenant dans le domaine d'aménagement des terrains pour le logement, a pu aménager 1094 ha de 1995 à 2014, à raison de 55 ha/an, répartis sur tous les gouvernorats de la République.

English gloss: the public housing land agency (AFH) serviced 1,094 ha in 1995-2014, about 55 ha per year nationwide.

p. 21:

> En dépit de la disproportion de la production des terres par rapport aux besoins, l'Agence Foncière d'Habitation a bien réussi à offrir des lotissements urbains pilotes [...] D'ailleurs, c'est ce qui a contribué à l'organisation de l'espace urbain et à la réduction de l'étalement anarchique des villes au détriment des terres agricoles.

English gloss: although its land output is out of proportion to needs, the AFH delivered model subdivisions, which the report says helped organise urban space and reduce unplanned sprawl onto farmland.
resolvedSources.notes: Official government report, but a policy document rather than a statistical publication; the 400 ha/yr figure has no stated method, year range or source. Page numbers are the printed page numbers.

resolvedSources.title: Studying Sharp Changes of Urban Landscape: Concession Within Agricultural, Hydraulic, and Maritime Public Domain in Kelibia City, Northern Tunisia
resolvedSources.publisher: Frontiers in Sustainable Cities 4:900336 (Kassouk Z., Hammami H., Ismail H.)
resolvedSources.extracts:
Abstract, p. 1:

> In southern Mediterranean countries, coastal urbanization often occurs on croplands. This expansion is frequently on most productive croplands and emerges as an important sustainability concern. [...] We describe the changes in urban structures during the period of 2012–2016 by using Multi dates Pleiades images [...] The results illustrated a dramatic increase of urban areas at the expense of agricultural land, maritime public domain (MPD) and hydraulic public domain (HPD). [...] For this reason, the implementation of systematic strategies for urban monitoring requires citizen awareness, law enforcement, and scientific supervision to mitigate land consumption, reduce flooding vulnerability, and to control the environmental impacts of urbanization.

Results, p. 6:

> In 2016, the urban area expanded by 65% from 2012. During this period, built-up areas over agriculture area are expanded by 400%.

> The results illustrated that the total increase of urban areas during the selected period reached over 300 Ha (Table 7).

Table 5, p. 7 ("Quantification of urban expansion at the expense of agricultural land, Maritime public domain and Hydraulic public domain"):

| | Maritime public domain | Hydraulic public domain | Agricultural land |
|---|---|---|---|
| Built-up areas in 2012 (Ha) | 16 | 5 | 13 |
| Built-up areas in 2016 (Ha) | 24 | 11 | 44 |

Table 7, p. 7: Total area (TA) of urban class 458 Ha (2012), 756 Ha (2016).

Discussion, p. 7:

> The problem is that planning design and urbanization norms should be reviewed, in particular the buffer zone surrounding the public domains.

English gloss (not needed, English source).
resolvedSources.notes: Single coastal town (Kelibia, Nabeul governorate, Cap Bon), four years. Table 5 (13 to 44 ha, roughly +240%) does not match the "400%" in the text; the table values are used. How "agricultural land" was delimited is not detailed in the extract.

resolvedSources.title: Data on Land Cover Transitions and Threats to Almond Tree Diversity in the Central-East of Tunisia (EasyChair Preprint 15880)
resolvedSources.publisher: EasyChair preprint (Ghenimi W., Gouta H., Geoffriau E., Carcaud N., Allouche Khebour F., Rejeb H.)
resolvedSources.extracts:
Abstract, p. 1:

> This study, based on satellite imagery (Landsat 5, 7, and 8) analyzed using QGIS, mapped the evolution of urbanization and the degradation of almond orchards between 1980 and 2023. In 1980, tree crops covered 3,234.2 hectares, while urban areas spanned 145 hectares. By 2012, urbanization reached 890 hectares, with a slight increase in tree crops (3,266.9 hectares). However, in 2023, a loss of 621 hectares of tree crops was recorded, while urbanization progressed by 46.83%, reaching 1,307.2 hectares.

Results, p. 3:

> By 2023, agricultural land further declined, with tree crops, including almonds, losing 621 hectares (18.99% compared to 2012), and vegetable and cereal crops decreasing by 111.1 hectares (29.58%) (Fig.2C). These losses were concentrated on the city's outskirts, where farmland was increasingly replaced by urban expansion, which surged from 890 hectares in 2012 to 1,307.2 hectares in 2014 (+ 46.83%). Orchard plots, especially those with almonds and intercropped olive trees, are being converted into residential and industrial zones. Additionally, persistent drought has exacerbated agricultural degradation in the region.

Table 2 (Kalâa Kebira delegation, 5,271 ha), 2012 to 2023 change: urban +417.2 ha; tree crops -621 ha; mixed crops -111.1 ha; pasture +314.7 ha (to 1,054.4 ha).
resolvedSources.notes: Unreviewed preprint, hence tier C. The template has no preprint type, so `institutional-report` is kept as the closest value. A Springer journal version exists but was not opened (paywalled). Internal errors: "2014" in the results text where the abstract and table say 2023; "83.72% increase" for 145 to 890 ha (the 83.7% is the share of 2012 urban area that is new, not an increase); mixed crops 1980-2012 given as -75.4 ha in text but -1,147 ha in the table. Between 2012 and 2023, urban area grew by 417 ha while 732 ha of crops were lost and pasture/uncultivated land grew by 315 ha, so not all crop loss is urbanisation; drought and abandonment also play a role.

resolvedSources.notes: FAOSTAT-based national aggregates. Agricultural land includes permanent pasture and permanent crops (olive expansion), so a gain in rangeland or olive plantations can mask the loss of high-value peri-urban plots. Arable land fell from 3.19 Mha (1980) to 2.77 Mha (2023), but these series do not attribute change to any cause; nothing here links the decline to urbanisation. Some values are carried forward: arable land 2020 = 2021 and 2022 = 2023; agricultural land 2022 = 2023 (2020 and 2021 differ slightly).

resolvedSources.title: Tunisie : Terres agricoles en péril
resolvedSources.extracts:
Lead:

> Les terres agricoles représentent 62% de la surface totale du pays. Mais chaque année, plus de 20 mille hectares disparaissent sous le double effet de l'érosion et de l'urbanisation.

English gloss: farmland is 62% of the country; over 20,000 ha disappear each year through erosion and urbanisation combined (no source given).

Section on Greater Tunis:

> dans le gouvernorat de la Manouba, 66,5 % des constructions ont été édifiées sur des zones d'interdictions, c'est-à-dire sur des périmètres publics irrigués, ou sur des forêts. Dans le gouvernorat de Ben Arous, près de 35% des constructions ont été édifiées sur des zones classées. Enfin, dans le gouvernorat de l'Ariana, elles sont estimées à plus de 50% [1]

English gloss: in Manouba 66.5% of constructions were built in prohibition zones, about 35% in classified zones in Ben Arous, over 50% in Ariana (footnote 1: AUGT studies; the base, all constructions or informal housing only, and the year are not stated).

> Les terres agricoles dont la vocation a été modifiée, ont été estimées par une étude en cours de la Direction Générale de l'Aménagement du Territoire, à 1370 hectares entre 2011 et 2021.

English gloss: agricultural land whose vocation was changed was estimated by an ongoing study of the Directorate General for Spatial Planning (DGAT) at 1,370 ha between 2011 and 2021. Geography not stated (context of the paragraph is Manouba/Greater Tunis).

Section "Un arsenal juridique inadapté ?":

> La perte globale des terres agricoles a été évaluée au milieu des années 1990 à environ 23 mille ha par an. Ces pertes, dont les causes sont principalement l'érosion et l'urbanisation, inquiètent les pouvoirs publics

English gloss: total farmland loss was estimated in the mid-1990s at about 23,000 ha per year, mainly from erosion and urbanisation.

Footnote [2], attached to this paragraph:

> [2] Elloumi M. Agriculture périurbaine et nouvelles fonctions du foncier rural en Tunisie. In : Elloumi M. (ed.), Jouve A.-M. (ed.), Napoléone C. (ed.), Paoli J.C. (ed.). Régulation foncière et protection des terres agricoles en Méditerranée. Montpellier : CIHEAM, 2011. p. 159-169 (Options Méditerranéennes : Série B. Etudes et Recherches; n. 66)

English gloss: the paragraph, including the 23,000 ha/yr estimate, draws on Elloumi (2011, CIHEAM). The footnote marker sits after the quoted phrase in the following sentence. Elloumi's paper itself could not be downloaded.

> Un arsenal juridique et institutionnel qui « ne semble pas avoir l'efficacité requise afin d'infléchir la progression de l'urbanisation aux dépens des terres agricoles »

English gloss: the legal framework "does not seem effective enough" to slow urbanisation on farmland (quoted from a cited academic article).
resolvedSources.notes: Investigative press. Figures are second-hand: the AUGT and DGAT studies were not found online. The 23,000 ha/yr figure dates from the mid-1990s and combines erosion with urbanisation. A secondary result (magef.org) suggests the Manouba 66.5% refers to the area of unplanned housing rather than all constructions; not verified.

resolvedSources.title: La Tunisie perd chaque année 25 mille hectares de terres agricoles
resolvedSources.extracts:
> Chaque année, 25 000 hectares de terres agricoles sont détruits en Tunisie sous le double effet de l'érosion et de l'activité humaine, dont l'urbanisation. En 30 ans, le pays perd à ce rythme l'équivalent de la surface du Cap bon en terre arables, estime l'économiste Radhi Meddeb

English gloss: each year 25,000 ha of farmland are destroyed by erosion and human activity, including urbanisation; at this rate the country loses the equivalent of Cap Bon in 30 years, says economist Radhi Meddeb.
resolvedSources.notes: Press report of an economist's statement, 3 February 2020; no source or method given. It is unclear whether the 25,000 ha figure is the economist's or the article's.

resolvedSources.title: Près de 72 % des Tunisiens vivent en milieu urbain
resolvedSources.extracts:
> Le taux d'urbanisation a atteint près de 72 % en Tunisie en 2025, tandis que la consommation de terres urbaines est estimée à environ 4 000 hectares par an, dont près de 40 % sont exploités dans le cadre d'une « expansion urbaine anarchique ».

English gloss: the urbanisation rate reached about 72% in 2025, and urban land consumption is estimated at about 4,000 ha per year, nearly 40% of it through "anarchic" (unplanned) urban expansion.
resolvedSources.notes: Figures presented by Dr Asma El Gharbi (university researcher, territorial development) at a CTFCI round table, as reported on 18 May 2026. The underlying study is not named, and the article does not say how much of the 4,000 ha is farmland.

resolvedSources.title: Rural under-development and internal migration: the example of Tunisian agriculture (Mediterra 2018, chapter 8)
resolvedSources.publisher: CIHEAM (Schwoob M.-H., IDDRI; Elloumi M., INRA Tunisia)
resolvedSources.extracts:
p. 170, "Impacts of urban coastal areas":

> The phenomenon is a source of pressure on agricultural land in peri-urban areas, some of which, as in Greater Tunis, correspond to land developed for irrigation (irrigated perimeter of the lower Medjerda valley built in the 1950s). Thus, according to the report on the environmental profile of Tunisia in 2012, urban pressure would cause Tunisia to lose between 2,000 and 3,000 ha of agricultural land every year (Euronet Consortium, 2012), the equivalent of one-tenth of the total area of the city of Tunis.

p. 171:

> The impact of agricultural activity on the soil in terms of erosion is particularly important, leading to losses of agricultural soil of 15,000 to 20,000 ha per year (Euronet Consortium, 2012).

Reference list, p. 179:

> Euronet Consortium (2012), Profil environnemental de la Tunisie, Bruwelles Euronet Consulting
resolvedSources.notes: Secondary citation: both figures come from the 2012 environmental profile of Tunisia (Euronet Consortium, EU-funded), which was not opened, so its method and reference years are unknown. The source separates urban losses (2,000-3,000 ha/yr) from erosion losses (15,000-20,000 ha/yr). The chapter's co-author Elloumi also wrote the CIHEAM 2011 paper cited by Nawaat (SRC-TG-850).
